assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is the segmentation-and-tiering method itself; creative concepting, channel buying and budget mechanics are out of scope
interest, engagement, reachability and incumbent signals are available, however imperfect, for the region under analysis
the claim that the medium tier is the opportunity is treated as an unproven hypothesis to be measured per niche (scope finding FP1), never a baked-in rule
exclusions: channel buying, bidding and budget allocation mechanics
individual-level identity resolution and PII handling
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for niche audience segmentation and opportunity tiering work units, grounded in classical segmentation theory, long-tail and superstar economics, and subcultural-capital sociology; no supplied dataset
source_citation: Smith 1956 'Product Differentiation and Market Segmentation as Alternative Marketing Strategies' (J. Marketing); Kotler & Keller STP (Segmentation-Targeting-Positioning) framework; Anderson 2006 'The Long Tail'; the Pareto principle (Pareto 1896 / Juran's 80-20); Thornton 1995 'Club Cultures: Music, Media and Subcultural Capital'; Bourdieu 1984 'Distinction: A Social Critique of the Judgement of Taste'; Rosen 1981 'The Economics of Superstars' (American Economic Review)

competency_questions.question: How is the regional crowd split by interest and what makes an operational, countable segment with measurable membership criteria?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INTEREST_PARTITION defines the interest partition and SEGMENT_DEFINITION gives a reproducible interest+geo membership predicate with a size estimate

competency_questions.question: How is insider niche membership (subcultural capital) and engagement depth distinguished from casual interest?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUBCULTURAL_CAPITAL grades insider-vs-casual and ENGAGEMENT_DEPTH measures intensity independently of size

competency_questions.question: How are the top-N entities per niche selected by salience?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOP_N_PER_NICHE ranks by salience (size x engagement x capital density) and selects a curve-adaptive top-N with floors

competency_questions.question: How is a segment's reachability and cost-to-reach assessed so existence is not confused with addressability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REACHABILITY maps channels, gatekeepers and cost-to-reach per segment with a fallback path

competency_questions.question: How is each niche mapped onto a head/middle/tail demand curve and split into fixed tier bands?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LONG_TAIL_VS_HEAD fits the demand curve and TIER_ASSEMBLY pre-registers the tier bands

competency_questions.question: How over-served (saturated) is a niche or tier, measured rather than asserted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SATURATION_SCORE measures supply density, share concentration and attention absorbed; LONG_TAIL_VS_HEAD locates the band

competency_questions.question: How is opportunity computed so an unreachable under-served pocket does not score high?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OPPORTUNITY_SCORE composes under_served x reachable; SATURATION_SCORE supplies the under-served side and REACHABILITY the reachable side

competency_questions.question: How is the economic (addressable) value of reaching a segment estimated net of reach cost?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADDRESSABLE_VALUE estimates value-per-member x propensity net of cost and OPPORTUNITY_SCORE folds it in

competency_questions.question: How is 'the medium tier is the opportunity' tested as a measured variable over pre-registered bands rather than assumed (FP1)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MEDIUM_TIER_HYPOTHESIS models tier as an independent variable and tests the opportunity-by-tier peak per niche; TIER_ASSEMBLY supplies the pre-registered bands

competency_questions.question: How is cross-niche audience overlap measured and corrected for double-counting?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CROSS_NICHE_OVERLAP estimates overlap, corrects tier totals and surfaces bridge audiences

competency_questions.question: How is segment drift monitored so a tier decision is re-measured before it ages out?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEGMENT_STABILITY estimates half-life and sets a per-segment re-measurement cadence

competency_questions.question: How are niches and tiers ranked against each other into a decision-ready shortlist?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NICHE_PRIORITIZATION combines opportunity, value, stability and overlap-corrected size into a ranked shortlist

competency_questions.question: How are false-positive opportunities screened on FP1 and the signals behind every score governed for provenance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FALSE_OPPORTUNITY_GUARD screens unreachable/artefactual/drifted/untested-medium-tier entries on FP1 and DATA_PROVENANCE governs source, bias and freshness

competency_questions.question: What does a downstream-ready activation brief contain, and how are predicted tiers back-tested and the FP1 criterion recalibrated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACTIVATION_HANDOFF packages scores, confidence, reach path and the tier verdict; BACKTEST_CALIBRATION back-tests predictions vs realized outcomes and recalibrates the model and FP1

glossary.definition: a mutually-intelligible split of a regional audience pool into interest domains and sub-domains (e.g. music->genres, sport->cricket)
the audience sharing a specific interest sub-domain and geographic scope with a measurable membership predicate
insider knowledge, taste hierarchies and 'hipness' that mark genuine scene membership (Thornton, after Bourdieu)
a measured degree to which a niche/tier's demand is already over-served by incumbents and absorbed attention
under_served x reachable x addressable_value: under-service alone is necessary but not sufficient
Anderson's demand curve where head is contested, extreme tail is unreachable, and the middle is the structural candidate band
the hypothesis that opportunity peaks in the medium tier, treated as a MEASURED variable per niche, never assumed (FP1)
whether a segment is contactable and activatable at acceptable cost via available channels and gatekeepers
an audience spanning two niches, surfaced by overlap analysis as its own opportunity surface
a ranked pocket that is unreachable, artefactual, drifted, or an untested medium-tier peak, rejected before a decision

nodes.definition: Partition a region's audience pool into mutually intelligible interest domains and then sub-domains (music -> rock/hip-hop/classical; sport -> cricket/football), so every subsequent segment, score and tier is computed within a defined interest taxonomy rather than over an undifferentiated crowd.

base.update_signal: interest taxonomy revised or a new top-level domain/sub-domain is added

included: domain and sub-domain partition of the regional pool

pros.claim: A defined interest partition makes every later metric (saturation, opportunity) computable per niche instead of over a meaningless aggregate
pros.example: music -> {rock, hip-hop, classical} lets cricket fans never dilute a rock-genre saturation count

cons.claim: A coarse or wrong taxonomy buries real niches inside an umbrella domain, so genuine opportunity is never measured
cons.example: lumping all 'electronic' into one bucket hides a thriving drum-and-bass micro-scene

failure_modes: interest domains overlap so an individual is double-counted across buckets
taxonomy too shallow to expose the niche where opportunity lives
folk taxonomy imposed top-down ignores how the audience self-describes
acceptance_tests: every audience member maps to at least one interest sub-domain and the partition covers the regional pool with documented overlap handling
revisit_triggers: a new interest domain emerges in the region
double-counting detected across buckets

nodes.definition: Define an operational segment as the audience sharing a specific interest sub-domain AND a geographic scope (and optionally a behavioural qualifier), with measurable membership criteria, so a 'segment' is a reproducible set you can count and reach, not a vibe.

base.update_signal: segment membership criteria or the interest+geo crossing rule changes

included: operational membership predicate (interest sub-domain AND geo)

pros.claim: An operational, criteria-based segment is reproducible and countable, so two analysts derive the same set and size
pros.example: 'cricket fans within 25km of Pune who attended a match in 12 months' is a fixed, re-runnable query

cons.claim: Over-specifying membership shrinks a segment below a usable scale and bakes in survey bias
cons.example: adding five behavioural qualifiers leaves 40 reachable people

failure_modes: segment defined by interest alone with no geo bound, so reach is unknowable
membership criteria not measurable from available signals
segment so narrow it is statistically unstable
acceptance_tests: each segment has a written membership predicate over available signals and a reproducible size estimate with a stated margin
revisit_triggers: available membership signals change
a segment size estimate moves beyond its stated margin

nodes.definition: Model the insider signals that mark genuine niche membership versus casual interest: vocabulary, taste hierarchies, scene gatekeeping and 'hipness' markers (Thornton's subcultural capital, after Bourdieu's cultural capital), so segments are graded by depth of belonging, not just stated topic.

base.update_signal: insider-signal vocabulary or the capital-grading rubric changes

included: subcultural capital indicators (lexicon, taste hierarchy, gatekeeping)

pros.claim: Grading by subcultural capital separates a deep, mobilizable core from drive-by interest, which predicts response far better than topic alone
pros.example: two 'jazz' followers split into a be-bop connoisseur and a someone who liked one playlist

cons.claim: Insider signals are noisy, gameable and culturally specific, so a rubric tuned on one scene mis-scores another
cons.example: 'authenticity' cues from a US punk scene misread an Indian indie scene

failure_modes: mistaking performative signaling for genuine capital
rubric encodes the analyst's taste as the scene's
insider lexicon shifts faster than the model updates
acceptance_tests: the capital rubric distinguishes insider from casual on a held-out labelled sample above an agreed accuracy floor
revisit_triggers: a scene's insider lexicon shifts
capital grading disagrees with scene-expert labels

nodes.definition: Within each niche, rank candidate audiences/communities by a salience score (size x engagement x subcultural-capital density) and select the top-N (e.g. top-5) per niche, so attention and budget concentrate on the few entities that carry each niche rather than its long tail of fragments.

base.update_signal: salience formula or the N cutoff per niche changes

included: ranking of communities/entities within a niche

pros.claim: A salience-ranked top-N concentrates finite effort on the entities that actually carry a niche, mirroring the Pareto concentration of attention
pros.example: top-5 cricket communities in a city capture most of the addressable, engaged fan base

cons.claim: A fixed N is arbitrary across niches of different shapes, truncating a flat niche and over-including a peaky one
cons.example: top-5 in a 3-community niche pads with noise; top-5 in a 50-community niche drops real players

failure_modes: salience dominated by raw size so a large-but-shallow audience outranks a small engaged core
fixed N truncates a legitimately broad niche
ranking unstable run-to-run
acceptance_tests: the top-N per niche is reproducible from the salience formula and each selected entity clears a minimum engagement and capital-density floor
revisit_triggers: salience weighting changes
a niche's shape makes a fixed N visibly wrong

nodes.definition: Assess whether a defined segment can actually be reached and activated: are there channels, gatekeepers, addressable inventory or owned access points through which the segment is contactable at acceptable cost? Opportunity that cannot be reached is not opportunity.

base.update_signal: available channels, inventory or gatekeeper access for a segment changes

included: channel and inventory mapping per segment

pros.claim: Pricing reachability turns 'is there demand?' into 'can we contact and activate them at acceptable cost?', which is what makes a tier actionable
pros.example: an under-served deep-house niche is real but only reachable via two private Discords, so cost-to-reach is high

cons.claim: Reachability is volatile (a platform change can strand a segment) and easy to over-estimate from gross inventory figures
cons.example: counting a platform's total users as reachable when targeting cannot actually isolate the niche

failure_modes: confusing audience existence with audience addressability
cost-to-reach computed from gross not net-of-targeting inventory
over-reliance on a single fragile channel
acceptance_tests: each segment carries a documented reach path with a cost-to-reach estimate and a fallback channel where the primary is fragile
revisit_triggers: a primary channel for a segment degrades or closes
cost-to-reach moves materially against the estimate

nodes.definition: Map each niche onto the demand-curve structure (Anderson's long tail over a Pareto/Zipf head): the head is over-served and contested, the extreme tail is real but too sparse to reach economically, and the middle band is the structural candidate region where reachable, under-served demand can exist.

base.update_signal: demand-curve shape parameters or the head/middle/tail band cutoffs change

pros.claim: Locating each niche on the head-middle-tail curve makes explicit WHY the middle is only a CANDIDate: head is contested, tail is unreachable, middle is where reachable under-served demand could sit
pros.example: a genre with a saturated top-10 and an unreachable 10,000-item tail leaves a navigable middle band

cons.claim: The long-tail framing can romanticize the tail; much of it is unreachable or non-existent demand, and curve shape varies wildly by niche
cons.example: treating every tail item as latent demand inflates opportunity for niches that are simply small

failure_modes: assuming a universal Pareto shape across niches of different curves
reading the middle band as automatically the opportunity (the very claim to be tested)
tail items with no real demand counted as latent
acceptance_tests: each niche has a fitted demand curve with head/middle/tail bands and the middle band is flagged as a candidate, not a conclusion
revisit_triggers: a niche's demand-curve shape changes
band cutoffs are disputed by downstream tier results

nodes.definition: Compute a saturation score per niche/tier: how over-served the demand already is, from supply density (number and strength of incumbents competing for the same audience), share concentration, and audience attention already absorbed, so 'crowded' becomes a measured quantity.

base.update_signal: saturation inputs (incumbent set, share data, attention proxy) or the formula change

pros.claim: A measured saturation score (incumbents x concentration x attention absorbed) replaces 'feels crowded' with a comparable number across niches and tiers
pros.example: head tier shows 12 strong incumbents and 80 percent attention share -> high saturation; a mid tier shows 3 weak ones -> low

cons.claim: Saturation is sensitive to how the competitor set is bounded; a too-narrow incumbent definition understates crowding
cons.example: ignoring substitute formats makes a saturated space look open

failure_modes: incumbent set drawn too narrowly so saturation is understated
attention proxy stale or platform-biased
high saturation conflated with high quality of incumbents
acceptance_tests: saturation scores are comparable across tiers, derived from a documented incumbent set, and re-derive within tolerance on a re-pull
revisit_triggers: the incumbent/competitor set definition changes
the attention proxy source changes

nodes.definition: Compute an opportunity score per niche/tier as a function of unmet/under-served demand AND reachability AND addressable value, explicitly as opportunity = under_served x reachable (low saturation is necessary but not sufficient), so an unreachable under-served pocket scores low, not high.

base.update_signal: opportunity formula, the under_served x reachable composition, or value weighting changes

included: opportunity = under_served x reachable x addressable_value

pros.claim: Defining opportunity as under_served x reachable prevents the classic error of calling a low-saturation but unreachable pocket an opportunity
pros.example: a deep niche with zero incumbents but no reach path scores near zero, not maximal

cons.claim: Multiplicative composition is brittle near zero and hides which factor drives the score, so a borderline reachability tanks a strong-demand niche
cons.example: a real opportunity with one fragile channel reads as no-opportunity

failure_modes: scoring under-served alone and ignoring reachability
value weighting that double-counts size already in saturation
multiplicative form masking the dominant factor
acceptance_tests: opportunity scores rank tiers reproducibly, an unreachable under-served tier scores low, and each score decomposes into its under_served, reachable and value factors
revisit_triggers: the reachability inputs change
the opportunity formula or its factor weights change

nodes.definition: Treat the claim 'the medium tier is the opportunity' as an UNPROVEN hypothesis to be MEASURED, not a baked-in rule: model tier (head/medium/tail or quantile bands) as an independent variable and test whether opportunity_score actually peaks at the medium tier, reporting the per-niche result and refusing to assume it (scope finding FP1).

base.update_signal: tier banding, the opportunity-by-tier test design, or the FP1 falsification criterion changes

included: explicit test of whether the peak is at the medium tier
per-niche accept/reject of the medium-tier claim

pros.claim: Encoding the medium-tier claim as a measured variable, not a rule, lets the data say 'yes here, no there' and protects against a confident but false default (FP1)
pros.example: in one genre opportunity peaks mid-curve; in another it peaks deep in the tail, and the model reports both rather than forcing 'medium'

cons.claim: Per-niche testing needs enough signal per tier or the curve is noise, and small niches cannot support a credible by-tier estimate
cons.example: a niche with three reachable communities cannot statistically locate an opportunity peak

failure_modes: baking 'medium tier = opportunity' in as an assumption rather than a tested result
reporting a tier peak without a confidence band
generalizing one niche's peak to all niches
acceptance_tests: the opportunity-by-tier result is reported per niche with a confidence band, and the medium-tier claim is accepted or rejected per niche against the FP1 falsification criterion, never assumed
revisit_triggers: a niche lacks enough per-tier signal to estimate the peak
the FP1 criterion or tier banding is revised

nodes.definition: Quantify the overlap of audiences across niches (people who belong to several at once) so segments are not treated as disjoint when they are not, double-counting is corrected, and bridge audiences spanning two niches are surfaced as their own opportunity surface.

base.update_signal: overlap measurement method or the bridge-audience definition changes

pros.claim: Measuring overlap corrects inflated totals and reveals bridge audiences (e.g. cricket+craft-beer) that are their own reachable opportunity
pros.example: correcting a 20 percent overlap stops two niches both claiming the same 10,000 people

cons.claim: Overlap estimation from sparse signals is error-prone, and aggressive de-duplication can erase a genuinely dual-affiliated person's value in both niches
cons.example: subtracting a fan from both niches understates each niche's real engaged base

failure_modes: treating niches as disjoint when they share large audiences
over-correcting overlap so dual members vanish
bridge audiences ignored as noise
acceptance_tests: overlap between scored niches is estimated and tier totals are corrected for double-counting with a stated method
revisit_triggers: overlap signal source changes
a bridge audience materially shifts a niche's corrected size

nodes.definition: Characterize how fast segments drift: interests, scene boundaries, sizes and reach paths change over time, so each segment carries a stability/half-life estimate and a re-measurement cadence, and a tier decision is timestamped rather than treated as permanent.

base.update_signal: observed drift rate or the re-measurement cadence policy changes

pros.claim: A stability estimate per segment turns a snapshot into a managed asset, flagging when a tier decision has aged out and must be re-pulled
pros.example: a fast-churning trend niche gets a 6-week cadence; a stable hobby niche gets a yearly one

cons.claim: Drift is hard to estimate without longitudinal data, and over-frequent re-measurement burns budget chasing noise
cons.example: re-scoring a stable niche monthly wastes effort and amplifies sampling jitter

failure_modes: treating a one-time segmentation as permanent
drift unmonitored until a campaign underperforms
cadence uniform across fast and slow niches
acceptance_tests: every segment carries a stability estimate and a re-measurement cadence, and stale decisions past their half-life are flagged
revisit_triggers: a segment drifts faster than its assigned cadence
longitudinal data revises a half-life estimate

nodes.definition: Estimate the economic value of reaching and converting each segment (size x conversion propensity x value-per-member, net of reach cost), grounding opportunity in superstar-economics realities (Rosen 1981: tiny quality/attention gaps yield outsized value concentration) so a tier's score reflects value, not just count.

base.update_signal: value-per-member model, conversion-propensity inputs or net-of-cost margin change

pros.claim: Pricing addressable value net of reach cost prevents chasing a large but low-value or expensive-to-reach segment, and surfaces superstar concentration where a small tier holds outsized value
pros.example: a small connoisseur tier with high value-per-member outscores a huge low-value casual tier

cons.claim: Value estimates compound several uncertain inputs (propensity, value-per-member, cost), so the score inherits wide error bars
cons.example: one optimistic conversion assumption swings the whole tier ranking

failure_modes: value driven by size alone ignoring per-member value
reach cost omitted so net value overstated
superstar concentration ignored, flattening real value differences
acceptance_tests: each segment's addressable value is net of reach cost and decomposes into size, propensity and value-per-member with stated error bars
revisit_triggers: conversion-propensity inputs change
value-per-member assumptions are revised

nodes.definition: Assemble the explicit tier structure per niche (head / medium / tail or quantile bands) from the demand curve and reachability, fixing band boundaries and membership so that saturation, opportunity and the medium-tier test all operate over the SAME, documented tier definition.

base.update_signal: tier band boundaries or the tiering method per niche changes

pros.claim: A single documented tier definition per niche ensures saturation, opportunity and the medium-tier test are computed over identical bands, making results comparable and the FP1 test honest
pros.example: fixing the 'medium' band once stops the opportunity test from silently re-banding to find a peak

cons.claim: Band boundaries are a modelling choice that can be gamed to manufacture or hide a medium-tier peak, so they must be pre-registered
cons.example: sliding the medium band until opportunity peaks there is circular reasoning

failure_modes: tier bands re-cut per metric so results are not comparable
boundaries chosen after seeing the opportunity curve
tiers assumed identical across differently shaped niches
acceptance_tests: tier bands are fixed and documented per niche before scoring, and the same bands feed saturation, opportunity and the medium-tier test
revisit_triggers: a niche's demand-curve shape forces a re-band
tier boundaries are disputed by the FP1 test outcome

nodes.definition: Rank niches (and tiers within them) against each other on a combined opportunity view (opportunity_score, addressable_value, stability, overlap-corrected size), producing the prioritized shortlist that the whole exercise exists to deliver.

base.update_signal: the cross-niche ranking criteria or their weights change

pros.claim: A single ranked shortlist combining opportunity, value, stability and corrected size turns many per-niche analyses into one decision-ready output
pros.example: a top-10 niche/tier shortlist ordered by net opportunity with stability flags

cons.claim: Combining several scores into one rank hides trade-offs and is sensitive to the weighting, so the same data yields different shortlists
cons.example: raising the value weight reshuffles the top of the list entirely

failure_modes: combining scores without exposing the weighting
ranking on stale (drifted) scores
ignoring overlap so two niches double-count the same audience at the top
acceptance_tests: the cross-niche ranking is reproducible from documented weights and each entry shows its component scores and stability flag
revisit_triggers: the ranking weights change
a top-ranked niche's underlying scores drift

nodes.definition: Measure engagement intensity within a segment (frequency, recency, contribution, advocacy) as distinct from segment size, so a small high-intensity core is not flattened against a large passive audience when computing salience and opportunity.

base.update_signal: engagement signals or the intensity index definition change

pros.claim: Separating intensity from size stops a large passive segment from outranking a small mobilizable core in salience and opportunity
pros.example: a 500-person superfan core outperforms a 50,000 passive list on response and is scored as such

cons.claim: Engagement signals are platform-specific and gameable, and high intensity in a tiny segment can be statistical noise
cons.example: a handful of very active accounts inflate a micro-segment's apparent intensity

failure_modes: intensity proxied by size
platform-specific signals treated as comparable across channels
noise from tiny samples read as real intensity
acceptance_tests: engagement intensity is measured independently of size and a small high-intensity core is distinguishable from a large passive audience
revisit_triggers: engagement signal sources change
intensity scores diverge from observed campaign response

nodes.definition: Govern the provenance and quality of the signals feeding every segment, score and tier: which platform/survey/panel each metric comes from, its bias and freshness, so saturation, opportunity and the medium-tier test inherit a documented, auditable evidence base rather than mixed unsourced numbers.

base.update_signal: a signal source is added, deprecated, or its bias/freshness profile changes

included: provenance trace from raw signal to tier score

pros.claim: A provenance registry makes every downstream score auditable and lets a stale or biased source be traced and quarantined before it corrupts a tier decision
pros.example: a tier built on a 2-year-old panel is flagged and down-weighted, not silently trusted

cons.claim: Provenance governance adds overhead and slows iteration, and perfect lineage is rarely achievable with third-party panel data
cons.example: chasing full lineage on a bought dataset stalls the analysis

failure_modes: mixing sources of different bias without annotation
stale signals trusted as current
no trace from a tier score back to its raw signals
acceptance_tests: every metric used in scoring is annotated with its source, freshness and known bias, and any tier score is traceable to its inputs
revisit_triggers: a signal source is deprecated or re-biased
a tier decision cannot be traced to its source signals

nodes.definition: Screen ranked opportunities for false positives before they reach a decision: low-saturation pockets that are unreachable, non-existent (artefactual) demand, drifted-away segments, or medium-tier peaks asserted without a passing FP1 test, so the shortlist carries only defensible opportunities.

base.update_signal: the false-opportunity screen criteria or the FP1 gate threshold change

pros.claim: A dedicated screen catches the four classic false opportunities (unreachable, artefactual, drifted, assumed-medium-tier) before budget is committed
pros.example: a thrilling 'untapped' niche is rejected because its demand is a scraping artefact and its medium-tier peak never passed FP1

cons.claim: An over-strict screen kills genuine but evidentially thin opportunities, biasing toward safe, already-known niches
cons.example: rejecting every niche without longitudinal data defaults the whole exercise back to the head

failure_modes: passing an opportunity that is under-served but unreachable
accepting a medium-tier claim without a passing FP1 test
artefactual demand surviving into the shortlist
acceptance_tests: every shortlist entry passes the false-opportunity screen, and any 'medium tier is the opportunity' claim is gated on a passing FP1 test
revisit_triggers: the FP1 gate threshold changes
a shipped opportunity later proves to be a false positive

nodes.definition: Package each prioritized, screened niche/tier into an activation brief: who the segment is, its insider context, its reach path and cost, its opportunity and value scores with confidence, and the explicit tier-claim verdict, so downstream creative/media teams act on a defensible, self-contained artefact.

base.update_signal: the activation brief contract or required fields change

pros.claim: A self-contained brief carrying scores, confidence, reach path and the tier verdict lets downstream teams act without re-deriving the analysis or re-introducing the medium-tier assumption
pros.example: the brief states 'opportunity peaks in the medium tier, FP1 passed, confidence 0.7, reach via two owned communities'

cons.claim: A brief frozen at handoff ages with segment drift, so a late-activated brief can act on a stale tier picture
cons.example: a brief shipped and used three months later misses a drifted reach path

failure_modes: brief omits confidence or the tier verdict so the assumption creeps back
scores handed off without provenance
brief used past its segment's half-life
acceptance_tests: each brief carries reach path, cost, opportunity/value scores with confidence, the tier verdict and a freshness date tied to the segment's half-life
revisit_triggers: the brief contract changes
a brief is consumed after its freshness date

nodes.definition: Close the loop by back-testing predicted opportunity/saturation/medium-tier verdicts against realized outcomes (response, conversion, value) and recalibrating the formulas and the FP1 criterion, so the whole tiering system is corrected by evidence rather than left as a one-shot heuristic.

base.update_signal: realized-outcome data arrives or the recalibration policy changes

pros.claim: Back-testing predicted tiers against realized response turns heuristic scores into calibrated ones and lets the medium-tier claim be confirmed or retired by evidence per niche
pros.example: after three campaigns the medium-tier peak holds for sport but is retired for music, updating FP1 priors

cons.claim: Outcomes are confounded (creative, timing, budget) so a clean attribution back to segmentation is hard, risking miscalibration on noisy signal
cons.example: a great campaign on a mediocre segment falsely validates the tier choice

failure_modes: calibrating on confounded outcomes
no feedback loop so errors persist across cycles
over-fitting the FP1 criterion to a few campaigns
acceptance_tests: predicted opportunity and tier verdicts are back-tested against realized outcomes and the formulas and FP1 criterion are recalibrated with the confound risks documented
revisit_triggers: realized-outcome data arrives
attribution confounds change the back-test interpretation

edges.why_related: engagement intensity is a salience input that constrains the top-N ranking
saturation scores are only as trustworthy as the provenance-governed signals feeding them
opportunity scores inherit the bias and freshness of their provenance-governed inputs
segment half-life sets the freshness date stamped on the activation brief
realized outcomes recalibrate the opportunity formula weights
outcome back-tests confirm or retire the medium-tier claim and update its FP1 priors per niche
uncorrected overlap inflates the audience attributed to a tier and distorts its saturation
value concentration by tier is co-evidence for where opportunity actually peaks

edges.resolution_rule: low saturation is necessary but not sufficient: never promote a low-saturation niche to high opportunity unless REACHABILITY clears the cost-to-reach floor; opportunity = under_served x reachable
edges.why_related: low saturation tempts a high opportunity score even when the niche is unreachable
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: pre-register tier band boundaries in TIER_ASSEMBLY before running the opportunity-by-tier test; reject any re-banding chosen after seeing the opportunity curve (prevents manufacturing an FP1 pass)
edges.why_related: sliding tier bands until opportunity peaks in the medium tier is circular and would fake the FP1 result
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: set N per niche from the fitted demand-curve shape rather than a global constant; a flat niche keeps fewer, a deep niche keeps more, so top-N does not truncate the very middle band under analysis
edges.why_related: a fixed global N conflicts with the per-niche curve shape and can truncate the candidate middle band
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: the false-opportunity screen overrides raw rank: a top-ranked niche that fails the unreachable/artefactual/drifted/untested-medium-tier screen is removed from the shortlist regardless of its score
edges.why_related: a high raw rank competes with screen rejection for the same shortlist slot
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

conflict_axes.name: under_served_vs_reachable
conflict_axes.description: A low-saturation niche looks like opportunity, but if it is unreachable the opportunity is illusory; under-service is necessary not sufficient.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: opportunity = under_served x reachable; gate on a cost-to-reach floor

conflict_axes.name: medium_tier_assumed_vs_measured
conflict_axes.description: The headline belief 'medium tier is the opportunity' is attractive as a rule but must be a measured per-niche result (FP1), or the whole tiering is circular.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pre-register bands; test the opportunity-by-tier peak; gate on FP1

conflict_axes.name: fixed_top_n_vs_curve_shape
conflict_axes.description: A constant N per niche is simple but truncates flat niches and over-includes peaky ones, distorting which entities carry a niche.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: derive N from the fitted demand curve per niche

conflict_axes.name: size_vs_intensity
conflict_axes.description: Salience and opportunity can be dominated by raw size, flattening a small high-intensity, high-capital core against a large passive audience.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: measure engagement intensity and subcultural capital independently of size

conflict_axes.name: overlap_correction_vs_double_value
conflict_axes.description: Correcting cross-niche overlap fixes inflated totals but can erase the genuine dual value of a person who really belongs to both niches.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: correct totals for ranking but credit dual members in each niche's engaged base

conflict_axes.name: snapshot_vs_drift
conflict_axes.description: A tier decision is a snapshot, but segments drift; treating it as permanent ages out the decision, while constant re-measurement burns budget on noise.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set re-measurement cadence per segment half-life

conflict_axes.name: screen_strictness_vs_missed_opportunity
conflict_axes.description: A strict false-opportunity screen protects the shortlist but biases toward already-known head niches; a loose screen lets false positives through.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate on FP1 and reachability but allow evidentially-thin niches into a watchlist tier

conflict_axes.name: provenance_rigor_vs_iteration_speed
conflict_axes.description: Strict signal provenance makes scores auditable but slows iteration, and perfect lineage is rarely available with third-party panels.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: annotate source/bias/freshness; quarantine stale sources without blocking the whole run

conflict_axes.name: value_concentration_vs_count
conflict_axes.description: Superstar economics means a small tier can hold outsized value, so ranking on count or size misreads where the real value sits.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: price addressable value net of reach cost and fold it into opportunity

edge_cases.description: A low-saturation niche is scored as high opportunity even though it is only reachable via two closed private communities at prohibitive cost.
edge_cases.trigger: opportunity scored from under-service alone, ignoring reachability
edge_cases.mitigation: compose opportunity = under_served x reachable and gate on a cost-to-reach floor

edge_cases.description: The medium tier is declared the opportunity by default and tier bands are quietly slid until the opportunity curve peaks there.
edge_cases.trigger: medium-tier claim assumed and tier bands re-cut after seeing results
edge_cases.mitigation: pre-register bands; test the by-tier peak; gate on a passing FP1 criterion

edge_cases.description: A fixed top-5 truncates a genuinely broad niche, dropping real players from the candidate middle band.
edge_cases.trigger: global constant N applied to a flat demand curve
edge_cases.mitigation: derive N per niche from the fitted demand-curve shape

edge_cases.description: A large passive audience outranks a small mobilizable superfan core because salience is dominated by raw size.
edge_cases.mitigation: measure intensity and subcultural capital independently of size

edge_cases.description: Two niches both claim the same overlapping audience at the top of the shortlist, double-counting reach and value.
edge_cases.trigger: niches treated as disjoint with no overlap correction
edge_cases.mitigation: estimate overlap, correct tier totals, and surface bridge audiences explicitly

edge_cases.description: A tier decision shipped months ago is activated against a segment whose reach path and size have drifted away.
edge_cases.trigger: activation brief used past the segment's half-life
edge_cases.mitigation: stamp briefs with a freshness date tied to the segment half-life and re-measure on cadence

edge_cases.description: An 'untapped' niche turns out to be a scraping/measurement artefact with no real demand, yet it tops the opportunity ranking.
edge_cases.trigger: artefactual demand not screened before ranking
edge_cases.mitigation: screen for artefactual demand and require provenance before an opportunity reaches the shortlist

edge_cases.description: Saturation is understated because the incumbent set was drawn too narrowly and ignored substitute formats.
edge_cases.mitigation: include substitutes in the incumbent definition and document the competitor-set boundary

edge_cases.description: A subcultural-capital rubric tuned on one scene mis-scores insiders in a culturally different scene.
edge_cases.trigger: insider-signal rubric applied across incompatible cultures
edge_cases.mitigation: validate the capital rubric per scene against scene-expert labels before use

edge_cases.description: The opportunity formula is calibrated on confounded campaign outcomes, so a great creative on a mediocre segment validates the wrong tier.
edge_cases.trigger: back-test attribution not controlled for creative/timing/budget confounds
edge_cases.mitigation: document confounds and require controlled attribution before recalibrating formulas or FP1

edge_cases.description: A small niche lacks enough per-tier signal, so the opportunity-by-tier peak is noise reported as a finding.
edge_cases.trigger: medium-tier test run on a niche with too few reachable entities per tier
edge_cases.mitigation: require a minimum per-tier sample and report a confidence band, else mark the test inconclusive

edge_cases.description: Stale third-party panel data silently feeds a saturation and opportunity score that drives a budget decision.
edge_cases.trigger: signal freshness not tracked in provenance
edge_cases.mitigation: annotate freshness per source and down-weight or quarantine stale signals

workflow.description: Split the regional audience pool into interest domains and sub-domains with documented overlap handling.
workflow.gate: every member maps to >=1 sub-domain; partition covers the pool

workflow.description: Specify each segment as interest sub-domain AND geo with a measurable membership predicate and size estimate.
workflow.gate: each segment has a reproducible predicate and sized estimate with a margin

workflow.description: Grade insider-vs-casual membership and engagement depth using a validated capital rubric.
workflow.gate: rubric clears the accuracy floor on a labelled held-out sample

workflow.description: Rank entities per niche by salience (size x engagement x capital density) and select a curve-adaptive top-N.
workflow.gate: selection reproducible; each entity clears engagement and capital floors

workflow.description: Map channels, gatekeepers and cost-to-reach per segment with a fallback path.
workflow.gate: each segment has a reach path, cost estimate and fallback

workflow.description: Fit the head/middle/tail demand curve per niche and pre-register the tier bands.
workflow.gate: bands fixed and documented before scoring; middle flagged candidate only

workflow.description: Measure over-service per tier from incumbent density, concentration and attention absorbed.
workflow.gate: scores comparable across tiers from a documented incumbent set

workflow.description: Compute opportunity = under_served x reachable x addressable_value per tier with factor decomposition.
workflow.gate: unreachable under-served tiers score low; scores decompose into factors

workflow.description: Test the opportunity-by-tier peak per niche over the pre-registered bands and accept/reject the medium-tier claim (FP1).
workflow.gate: per-niche verdict with a confidence band; claim never assumed

workflow.description: Rank niches/tiers on combined opportunity, value, stability and overlap-corrected size.
workflow.gate: ranking reproducible from documented weights with component scores shown

workflow.description: Screen the shortlist for unreachable, artefactual, drifted, and untested-medium-tier false positives.
workflow.gate: every entry passes the screen; medium-tier claims gated on FP1

workflow.description: Package each surviving niche/tier into a self-contained activation brief with scores, confidence, reach path, tier verdict and freshness date.

dominance_rules.rule: INTEREST_PARTITION and SEGMENT_DEFINITION must be fixed before any saturation or opportunity score is computed
dominance_rules.rationale: scores are meaningless without a defined niche and a countable segment
dominance_rules.trigger: scoring begins without a fixed partition and segment register
dominance_rules.action: block scoring until partition and segments are defined

dominance_rules.rule: OPPORTUNITY_SCORE must include REACHABILITY as a multiplicative factor, never under-service alone
dominance_rules.rationale: an unreachable under-served pocket is not an opportunity
dominance_rules.action: require under_served x reachable composition with a cost-to-reach floor

dominance_rules.rule: TIER_ASSEMBLY bands must be pre-registered before MEDIUM_TIER_HYPOTHESIS is tested
dominance_rules.rationale: re-banding after seeing the opportunity curve manufactures a false FP1 pass
dominance_rules.trigger: tier bands changed after the by-tier test is run
dominance_rules.action: reject post-hoc re-banding and re-run on the pre-registered bands

dominance_rules.rule: The medium-tier claim must carry a per-niche verdict with a confidence band and must not be asserted as a default
dominance_rules.rationale: FP1: 'medium tier is the opportunity' is a measured variable, not a rule
dominance_rules.trigger: the medium tier is treated as the opportunity without a passing test
dominance_rules.action: mark the niche inconclusive until the by-tier test passes FP1

dominance_rules.rationale: a high score that fails the false-positive screen is not a real opportunity
dominance_rules.trigger: a top-ranked entry fails the unreachable/artefactual/drifted/untested screen
dominance_rules.action: remove the entry from the shortlist regardless of rank

dominance_rules.rule: TOP_N_PER_NICHE must derive N from the fitted demand curve, not a global constant
dominance_rules.rationale: a fixed N truncates flat niches and over-includes peaky ones
dominance_rules.trigger: a global constant N applied across niches of different shapes
dominance_rules.action: set N per niche from LONG_TAIL_VS_HEAD curve fit

dominance_rules.rule: Every score must be traceable to a provenance-governed signal before it drives a decision
dominance_rules.rationale: unsourced or stale signals corrupt tier decisions invisibly
dominance_rules.action: block the score from the shortlist until provenance is attached

dominance_rules.rule: Activation briefs must carry a freshness date tied to SEGMENT_STABILITY half-life
dominance_rules.rationale: a drifted segment makes a frozen brief act on a stale picture
dominance_rules.trigger: a brief is consumed past its freshness date
dominance_rules.action: require re-measurement before the brief is activated

dominance_rules.rule: BACKTEST_CALIBRATION must control for creative/timing/budget confounds before recalibrating formulas or FP1
dominance_rules.rationale: confounded outcomes validate the wrong tier
dominance_rules.action: require controlled attribution before changing weights or FP1

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not score saturation or opportunity before the interest partition and segments are fixed; re-scoring after a partition change is total rework
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-running all tier scores after a late taxonomy revision

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not bake in 'medium tier = opportunity'; retrofitting the FP1 measured-variable test after assuming it requires re-deriving every tier verdict
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unwinding a baked-in medium-tier assumption across all niches

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not score opportunity from under-service alone; adding reachability after the fact reshuffles the whole ranking
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-ranking the shortlist once unreachable pockets are removed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not re-cut tier bands after seeing the opportunity curve; pre-register them or the FP1 test must be re-run from scratch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-running the by-tier test after a circular re-banding is caught

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not apply a global fixed N across niches; correcting truncated niches later means re-selecting and re-scoring them
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-selecting top-N for every flat niche after truncation is found

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not mix unsourced signals into scores; attaching provenance retroactively means re-validating every affected tier
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-validating tier scores after an unsourced signal is discovered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not ignore cross-niche overlap; de-duplicating after ranking changes the top of the shortlist
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-ranking after overlap inflation is found at the top of the list

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not ship activation briefs without a freshness date; chasing drift after activation means re-measuring mid-campaign
anti_rework_rules.prevents: emergency re-measurement of a drifted segment mid-flight

iteration_protocol.trigger: a low-saturation niche is flagged as high opportunity but proves unreachable in practice
iteration_protocol.action: re-weight REACHABILITY in OPPORTUNITY_SCORE and tighten the cost-to-reach floor

iteration_protocol.trigger: the medium-tier claim is being asserted as a default rather than measured
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the by-tier test over pre-registered bands in MEDIUM_TIER_HYPOTHESIS and enforce the FP1 gate in FALSE_OPPORTUNITY_GUARD

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fixed top-N visibly truncates a broad niche
iteration_protocol.action: switch TOP_N_PER_NICHE to a curve-adaptive N from the LONG_TAIL_VS_HEAD fit

iteration_protocol.trigger: a large passive audience outranks a small engaged core
iteration_protocol.action: re-measure ENGAGEMENT_DEPTH and SUBCULTURAL_CAPITAL independently of size and re-weight salience

iteration_protocol.trigger: two top-ranked niches double-count the same audience
iteration_protocol.action: re-estimate CROSS_NICHE_OVERLAP and correct NICHE_PRIORITIZATION totals

iteration_protocol.trigger: an activated brief acts on a drifted segment
iteration_protocol.action: shorten the re-measurement cadence in SEGMENT_STABILITY and re-stamp ACTIVATION_HANDOFF freshness dates

iteration_protocol.trigger: a shipped opportunity proves to be a false positive after the campaign
iteration_protocol.action: strengthen the FALSE_OPPORTUNITY_GUARD screen and recalibrate the formulas and FP1 in BACKTEST_CALIBRATION

priority_rationale: INTEREST_PARTITION/SEGMENT_DEFINITION and signal provenance are foundational; reachability and the demand-curve/tier structure gate scoring; SATURATION_SCORE and OPPORTUNITY_SCORE feed the measured MEDIUM_TIER_HYPOTHESIS (FP1); prioritization, false-opportunity screening, activation and back-test calibration close the method.
